$comment: Shared conformance corpus for every Latch Vector SSO SDK.
Derived from ../CONTRACT.md. When this file and the service disagree, the service wins.
Each SDK has one test that reads this file, builds every token locally from keys.json,
feeds it to its own verifier, and asserts the same outcome. Identical behaviour across
five languages stops being a belief and becomes something CI proves.
FORMAT
base        which claim template to start from: "user" or "client".
claims      overrides merged over the template. A null value DELETES that claim.
verify      which entry point to call: "user" (verify) or "client" (verifyClient).
sign.key    "primary" (the key in jwks.json) or "attacker" (an unrelated key).
sign.alg    signing algorithm. Default RS256.
sign.header extra JOSE header members.
mutate      post-signing tampering, see MUTATIONS below.
expect      "accept" or "reject".
reason      why. Reject reasons are grouped by the CONTRACT check they enforce.
principal   expected fields when expect is accept.
reach       canReach() assertions: path -> expected boolean.
TIME
A claim value that is a string matching ^[+-][0-9]+$ is an offset in seconds from
the moment the test runs. "+900" = now + 15min. Keeps the corpus from expiring.
MUTATIONS
alg_none              re-encode the header with alg=none and drop the signature.
alg_hs256_public_key  re-sign with HS256 using the PUBLIC key as the HMAC secret.
tamper_payload        flip uid to 1 after signing, keep the original signature.
strip_signature       header.payload. with an empty signature segment.
truncate_signature    drop the last 8 characters of the signature.
garbage               not a JWT at all.
empty                 the empty string.
whitespace            a string of spaces.
huge                  a ~10MB token. Must be rejected without exhausting memory.
padClaimBytes         NOT a mutation: pads the payload with a filler claim of this many
bytes BEFORE signing, producing a token that is genuinely
well-formed and validly signed, and merely enormous.
VERIFIER CONFIGURATION under which these outcomes hold
issuer  https://sso.example.com
audience https://api.example.com
clockToleranceSeconds 30

vectors.name: user_valid
vectors.reason: The happy path. All four mandatory checks pass.

vectors.name: user_aud_array_contains_ours
vectors.reason: aud is a list in the spec. Ours being the second entry is still a match.

vectors.name: user_aud_single_element_array
vectors.reason: The service issues aud as a one-element array. This is the real wire shape.

vectors.name: user_unknown_claims_ignored
vectors.reason: CONTRACT 3: a customer may add their own claim names. An unknown claim is not a signal and must not be enforced or rejected.

vectors.name: user_expired_inside_clock_tolerance
vectors.reason: 29s past expiry with a 30s tolerance is still valid. Clock skew between our servers and theirs is real.

vectors.name: user_subtree_scope
vectors.reason: A subtree grant reaches the node itself and everything beneath it.

vectors.name: user_subtree_must_not_leak_to_sibling_by_prefix
vectors.reason: THE prefix trap. A naive startsWith on an unterminated path would let /1/5/ reach /1/57/ — a different company. The trailing slash is what makes the prefix test a segment test. Any SDK that normalises paths differently leaks across organizations here.

vectors.name: user_subtree_grant_without_trailing_slash_must_not_widen
vectors.reason: Defence in depth on the prefix trap. The service always emits a trailing slash, so a grant of /1/5 should never appear — but if one ever did, a raw startsWith would hand /1/57/ to a caller granted /1/5/. The grant is normalised before comparison so that a malformed claim narrows the reach rather than widening it. An SDK that trusts the claim verbatim fails this vector, and the failure is a cross-organization read.

vectors.name: user_tenant_root_subtree
vectors.reason: CONTRACT 3: /1/ grants /1/57/903/. Tenant-wide reach.

vectors.name: user_no_permissions
vectors.reason: A user with no permissions at this application is authenticated but authorized for nothing. Not an error.

vectors.name: user_permissions_wrong_type_fails_closed
vectors.reason: A malformed permissions claim must degrade to NO permissions, never to the string being treated as one. Fail closed, do not throw: the token itself is validly signed.

vectors.name: user_scope_claims_absent
vectors.reason: scope_subtree is present only when the reach extends below. Absent claims are empty lists, and reach nothing.

vectors.name: client_valid
vectors.reason: Machine token happy path.

vectors.name: client_unbound_has_no_application_id
vectors.reason: An unbound client carries no application_id. The field is absent, not zero.

vectors.name: client_empty_scope
vectors.reason: A client with no scopes may do nothing. Authenticated, not authorized.

vectors.name: reject_forged_signature
vectors.reason: CHECK 1 signature. Signed by a key that is not in the JWKS. Anyone can mint tokens without this.

vectors.name: reject_alg_none
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. alg:none must be rejected before the signature is examined.

vectors.name: reject_alg_confusion_hs256_with_public_key
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. The public key is published at the JWKS endpoint. If HMAC algorithms are not pinned out, an attacker signs with the public key as the shared secret and the verifier accepts it.

vectors.name: reject_tampered_payload
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. uid changed after signing. The signature no longer covers the payload.

vectors.name: reject_stripped_signature
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. An empty signature segment is not a valid RS256 signature.

vectors.name: reject_truncated_signature
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. Malformed signature must fail verification, not crash the parser.

vectors.name: reject_unknown_kid
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. Claiming a trusted kid while signing with another key. The kid selects which published key to check against; it is not itself evidence.

vectors.name: reject_jku_header_points_at_attacker
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. Keys come from the issuer's discovery document, never from a URL the token itself supplies. An SDK that honours jku hands key selection to the attacker.

vectors.name: reject_x5u_header_points_at_attacker
vectors.reason: CHECK 1. Same as jku for the X.509 variant.

vectors.name: reject_wrong_issuer
vectors.reason: CHECK 2 issuer. A validly signed token from another deployment must not be accepted here.

vectors.name: reject_missing_issuer
vectors.reason: CHECK 2. No issuer is not the same as the right issuer.

vectors.name: reject_wrong_audience
vectors.reason: CHECK 3 audience. THE most consequential check. This token is validly signed by a trusted issuer and has the right iss, so checks 1 and 2 both pass. Without check 3, every user of every other application on the platform can authenticate as themselves against yours.

vectors.name: reject_missing_audience
vectors.reason: CHECK 3. An absent aud matches nothing.

vectors.name: reject_aud_array_without_ours
vectors.reason: CHECK 3. Membership in the list is the test, and we are not in it.

vectors.name: reject_aud_substring_not_match
vectors.reason: CHECK 3. Audience comparison is equality, never a prefix or substring test. A domain that merely starts with ours is a different application.

vectors.name: reject_mfa_pending_token
vectors.reason: CHECK 4 token_use. The real shape of a pending token: same key, same issuer, no aud. It means the password was right and the second factor has NOT been proven.

vectors.name: reject_mfa_pending_even_with_correct_audience
vectors.reason: CHECK 4, the whole reason it exists. A pending token carrying a valid aud passes checks 1-3. Only the explicit token_use check stops a half-finished login from being accepted as a full one. This vector fails for any SDK that relies on the audience check as a side effect.

vectors.name: reject_client_token_at_user_verifier
vectors.reason: CHECK 4. A machine is not a person: no uid, no permissions. It must never arrive at the user verifier.

vectors.name: reject_user_token_at_client_verifier
vectors.reason: CHECK 4 mirrored. Authorization for a machine is by scope; a user token has permissions instead and must not be read as a client.

vectors.name: reject_missing_token_use
vectors.reason: CHECK 4. Absent is not access. Fail closed.

vectors.name: reject_token_use_wrong_case
vectors.reason: CHECK 4. The comparison is exact. A case-insensitive match is a wider door than the contract describes.

vectors.name: reject_token_use_unknown_value
vectors.reason: CHECK 4. Only the three documented kinds exist, and only one of them is an access token.

vectors.name: reject_expired
vectors.reason: Lifetime. An hour past expiry.

vectors.name: reject_expired_just_outside_tolerance
vectors.reason: Lifetime, and a deliberate trap for .NET: TokenValidationParameters defaults ClockSkew to FIVE MINUTES. An SDK that does not set it explicitly accepts this token while the other four reject it — the same credential, two answers.

vectors.name: reject_not_yet_valid
vectors.reason: Lifetime. nbf five minutes out is well past any sane skew allowance.

vectors.name: reject_missing_exp
vectors.reason: Lifetime. A token that never expires is not a token this service issues.

vectors.name: reject_uid_missing
vectors.reason: Claim shape. uid IS the identity. Without it there is no one to be.

vectors.name: reject_uid_as_string
vectors.reason: Claim shape. A string uid means something upstream is not what we think it is. Refuse rather than coerce — silent coercion is how a 4711 becomes a 47.

vectors.name: reject_org_id_missing
vectors.reason: Claim shape. org_id is the active company and every scoping decision downstream depends on it.

vectors.name: reject_org_id_as_string
vectors.reason: Claim shape, and the highest-consequence one: a coerced org_id is a cross-organization data leak.

vectors.name: reject_tenant_id_missing
vectors.reason: Claim shape. tenant_id scopes the data layer.

vectors.name: reject_client_org_id_missing
vectors.reason: Claim shape. org_id is the attribution — which customer the machine acts for.

vectors.name: reject_client_wrong_audience
vectors.reason: CHECK 3 applies identically to machine tokens: a client bound to an application carries that application's identifier as aud.

vectors.name: reject_client_forged_signature
vectors.reason: CHECK 1 on the machine path. The client verifier is not a relaxed verifier.

vectors.name: reject_garbage
vectors.reason: Input handling. Not a JWT. Must fail as a verification error, not an unhandled parse exception.

vectors.name: reject_empty_string
vectors.reason: Input handling. The empty string is the shape a missing header has after naive trimming.

vectors.name: reject_whitespace
vectors.reason: Input handling.

vectors.name: reject_huge_token
vectors.reason: Input handling. ~10MB of base64. Must be refused promptly and without exhausting memory — an unauthenticated caller controls this size.

vectors.name: reject_oversized_but_valid_token
vectors.reason: Size ceiling, and the one that needs no forgery at all. Unlike reject_huge_token this is a REAL token: correctly signed by the trusted key, right issuer, right audience, right token_use. It is simply 100KB. An unauthenticated caller picks that number, so without a ceiling checked BEFORE decoding, every request costs CPU and memory proportional to whatever they send. A real token is under 8KB; CONTRACT.md section 2 sets the limit at 64KB.
